newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $271 mln trade gap in May.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $271 mln trade gap in May.

text.p: Brazil posted a $271 million trade deficit in May, with exports of $4.658 billion and imports of $4.929 billion, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said.
The ministry said in a statement that average daily exports were $232.9 million and average daily imports were $246.5 million during the month.
The May result brings Brazil's year-to-date trade gap to $4.26 billion. Economists expect the gap will top $11 billion by the end of the year.

It was Brazil's best monthly trade figure since a $269 million surplus in May 1996. April and May are Brazil's best exporting months, a period when the nation exports the bulk of its agricultural crop.
